how_to_read: 1. Read the head first: the first 34 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=34, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' compact-toast-tracker.metadump.json).
2. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' compact-toast-tracker.metadump.json
3. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' compact-toast-tracker.metadump.json
4. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' compact-toast-tracker.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
5. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' compact-toast-tracker.metadump.json returns whole entries.

essence.one_sentence: A parcel's state is a fact people glance at many times, so the most useful surface answers it before anyone opens it.
essence.summary: Dark floating surface: status word on the face (ETA where it fits), checkpoints behind one toggle, status changes announced without taking focus, and a way back after dismiss.

formula.full: one floating status surface (a persistent panel, or a transient snackbar) + status word face with ETA where room allows + expandable checkpoint steps + copy, open-carrier and dismiss, with a return path chosen from dv-dismiss-return + dark surfaces stepped lighter with hairlines
formula.essential: status word over a glanceable face, steps behind a toggle

angles.text: The face is a small pill that answers the question with a word; the steps wait for the curious.
Expanded, the body reads as a carrier ledger: each stage in its own wording, with a next step for the shopper.
Depth comes from one step of lighter surface and a hairline, so the surface lifts without a glow or a shadow stack.
The interesting moment is the status update: a pulse, a reappearing toast or a silent swap each tells a different story.

a status change that does not pull focus
a change that brings the surface back up
a 24 px or 44 px hit area

poles: dismiss ends the surface and nothing returns it

llm_brief.text:
On the table: a dark, very compact, collapsible toast UI menu that tracks one shipped parcel, in the user's words: "a dark mode, very compact collapsible toast UI menu for tracking a package". In this build a toast can read several ways: a persistent floating status panel over the page (one reading, the default), a transient snackbar that enters from an edge and times out (one line, zero or one text action, no icons, per Material), a stack of toasts, an inline edge bar, a status-only face, a full timeline, or a tracking-number form. The face can carry the status word alone or with the ETA. The body can hold the checkpoint steps and the copy, open-carrier and dismiss controls. Carrier vocabulary (researched on UPS and Ship24 pages): Label Created, Shipped or On the Way, Out for Delivery, Delivered, Exception; a detail line names the cause, and each status pairs with a shopper action. Sourced numbers: pointer targets at least 24 by 24 CSS px (44 px enhanced), body text at 4.5 to 1 contrast, meaningful non-text marks at 3 to 1, and interaction-triggered motion that can be turned off.
Ways in: the glance (a status word, with the ETA where it fits, carries the face); the ledger (checkpoints as a stepper with the wording of each stage); the quiet dark (surfaces one step lighter with hairlines, no glow); the change (a status update shown as a pulse, a flash, a reappearing toast, or a silent swap); the way back (after dismiss: an edge tab, a return on the next status change, or hidden until reload).
Dials: collapsed face 32 to 40 px tall pill, 40 to 48 px edge strip, or 200 to 240 px wide card; expand about 200 to 300 ms ease-out, with collapse a little shorter; a transient toast about 4 to 10 s before it times out (search snippets, unconfirmed).
Worn paths: the usual move is a rounded alert box with a bell and a red X; fresher: a status word with a shape, and no red X in transit. The usual move is neon outlines or a violet gradient; fresher: a hairline and one lighter step. The usual move is a wide bottom bar with large headline type; fresher: a corner pill or an edge strip. The usual move is emoji as status icons; fresher: a word or a shape. The usual move is pure white text on pure black; fresher: off-white on near-black. The usual move is a step list that opens on hover alone; fresher: a button that works by keyboard and touch. The usual move is 12 to 16 px toggles; fresher: 24 px or more.
Open: stack, data and platform default to plain HTML, CSS and JS in one file with no external requests, a hard-coded sample package whose status can be changed in the page, and a layout that works at 375 px and at desktop width; language defaults to English with one generic carrier name. Status data shapes (a flat record, a fixed status set, free carrier text, a separate exception field) and checkpoint and ETA formats are options.

ak-red-x.instead: A status dot in its hue with a word beside it, or an amber triangle for a real problem.

ak-neon-purple.instead: A flat tinted slate or charcoal surface with one hairline edge in the status hue, or a warm graphite panel.

ak-emoji-shadow.term: emoji status icons and per-element shadow
ak-emoji-shadow.instead: 16 px SVG glyphs on one stroke weight, or a plain word; shadow only on the floating panel.

ak-hover-only.instead: Tap or Enter toggles with aria-expanded; hover may preview the step list but never be the only path.

ak-pure-white-black.instead: Off-white text near #E6E8EC on a graphite or #0b0b0d surface, checked at 4.5:1 or better.

ak-noise-stunning.instead: Name the specific thing: the status word, the carrier wording or the action.

ak-full-width-bar.term: full-width bottom bar with large headline type
ak-full-width-bar.instead: Corner pill 32 to 40 px, edge strip 40 to 48 px, or 200 to 240 px card.

ux_principles._about: Discipline rungs for UI and interaction design, applied to a compact dark status toast. Principles from practice; options, not requirements.

ux-fitts-targets.text: Time to reach a target grows with distance and shrinks with size, so the expand toggle and dismiss control should be the largest hit areas in the panel.
behaviors: A dismiss control in a corner, sized at least 24 px, is cheap to reach
The collapsed pill itself is the biggest target, so the whole face toggles
ux-fitts-targets.principle: Reach cost is distance divided by size; put the frequent controls near the thumb or the edge and make them big.

ux-hick-gestalt.text: Decision time rises with the number of choices, and items that sit close or look alike read as one group.
behaviors: Three actions (copy, open carrier, dismiss) fit one row; more push a menu
ETA sits next to the status word so they read as one fact
ux-hick-gestalt.principle: Fewer visible choices and clear groups make the panel scan in one glance.

ux-heuristics-jakob.term: system status and recognition over recall
ux-heuristics-jakob.text: Nielsen's visibility of system status and recognition-over-recall heuristics, with Jakob's law: users expect a notification to behave like the ones they already know.
behaviors: The collapsed face shows the current status word without expanding
Expanded steps use the carrier's familiar wording, so no decoding is needed
ux-heuristics-jakob.principle: Show the state at a glance; do not make the user remember it or learn a new pattern.

ux-dos-donts-mistakes.term: compact floating panel dos, don'ts and mistakes
ux-dos-donts-mistakes.text: Common mistakes for small floating panels: covering page content, hover-only controls, and status changes that happen silently.
dos: Keep one panel, one primary action
Let the collapsed face carry the status
Give the status change a visible and announced cue
donts: Do not hide the dismiss control behind hover
Do not stack several floating panels in one corner
Do not let the panel block the page's own dismiss or close controls
signals: two toasts fight for one corner

accessibility._about: Confirmed numbers from fetched WCAG 2.2 Understanding pages; 44 px and aria details are inferred.

a11y-motion.text: Motion triggered by interaction must be disableable unless essential; honor prefers-reduced-motion for expand, collapse and status pulses.
behaviors: Under reduced motion, expand and collapse become an instant swap
A status pulse becomes a colour or icon change, not movement

a11y-contrast.text: Body text needs 4.5:1 against its background; meaningful non-text cues (status dots, progress segments, icons) need 3:1.
behaviors: Secondary grey text on charcoal must still reach 4.5:1
Each status hue needs 3:1 against the surface it sits on

a11y-target-size.text: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS px, or spaced so a 24 px circle around each misses the others; 44 px is the enhanced size.
behaviors: A 16 px chevron needs padding to a 24 px hit area
Dismiss at 24 px minimum; 44 px if it is the main control

a11y-disclosure-live.text: Whichever collapsible reading is chosen, its state reaches assistive tech, and a status change goes to an aria-live polite region without moving focus.
behaviors: Chevron reading: a button with aria-expanded that flips on each toggle
Header-click reading: the header row is the button and carries aria-expanded
Drag-handle reading: exposes its position as a separator, not a disclosure
Auto-collapse and badge readings have no toggle, so the live region alone announces the change
A status change announces politely, once, and does not repeat on every render
a11y-disclosure-live.principle: Announce what changed without moving focus; the state of the chosen collapse reading needs to reach keyboard and screen reader users.

tracking._about: Carrier tracking pages: the status vocabulary, exception wording and the date line, from fetched carrier and tracking-blog pages.

tr-status-words.text: Carriers share a short set of status words; UPS pages list the common ones, and the pages show current location, status and expected delivery date together.
behaviors: Label Created: the carrier does not yet have the parcel
Out for Delivery: on a vehicle today, the stage with the most shopper attention
signals: a date line next to the status

tr-exception.text: Exception is the catch-all for anything off the expected path; the detail line gives the cause.
signals: a cause line under the exception word

tr-shopper-action.text: Ship24 pairs each status with a shopper action, such as checking delivery instructions for Out for Delivery.
tr-shopper-action.principle: A status is more useful with the next thing to do beside it.

patterns._about: Compact panels and toasts: target size, dark surfaces, contrast and timing. Specifics come from fetched standards pages unless marked inferred.

pt-dark-surface.text: Material's dark theme labels the background 0dp and each surface 1dp, with a surface overlay on each; primaries are desaturated to keep 4.5:1 body-text contrast.

pt-dark-elevation-inferred.text: One reading of elevation on dark: a higher surface sits a step lighter than the page instead of casting a shadow.
behaviors: A floating panel could be one step lighter than the page instead of casting a shadow

island_states._about: Options and readings from one found page (cult-ui Dynamic Island docs). The page gives preset names and intended uses only; no pixel footprints or durations are printed on it.

sc-presets.text: Fourteen named shape presets, each with one intended use, set through setSize or initialSize; the page prints no width, height or radius for them.
properties: reset and empty: internal or hidden
signals: presets object exposes raw dimensions at runtime
sc-presets.quote: Use these built-in shape presets with setSize(...) or initialSize.

sc-compact-readings.text: The page has no very compact preset; the three compact presets are three readings of small, side by side.

readings.in_practice: compact preset: a row with a label and a title
compactLong: compact but wider row
compactMedium: medium compact card

sc-transitions.text: Two ways to change size: an immediate setSize switch, or a queued sequence where each step waits a delay before it runs.
behaviors: setSize switches to the preset at once
A queued step waits its delay in milliseconds before the next size
isAnimating is true while a queued sequence runs, so controls can be disabled
sc-transitions.quote: delay is the wait time (in milliseconds) before each step.

sc-collapse-motion.text: The page describes the island as expanding and collapsing in place and wrapping each state view with enter and exit motion; no easing or duration is given.
behaviors: Each state view gets its own enter and exit motion through DynamicContainer
Motion is the library the page names for the morph
sc-collapse-motion.quote: Use it for notifications, media controls, timers, or status updates that expand and collapse in place.

toast_behavior._about: Material Design 1 snackbars (its term for a toast-style notice), scraped from one page. Facts from the page; the toast mapping is a search alias.

options._about: options, not requirements: how a dismissed panel comes back

dv-dismiss-return.text: Dismiss removes the panel, so without another route the user has no way back until a reload. Three ways back, each with what fits it.

choices.choice: small reopen tab on the edge
choices.fits_when: the user may dismiss by habit and still wants to recover quickly; a tab of 24 px or more stays reachable

choices.choice: reappears on the next status change
choices.fits_when: the parcel is still moving and the user needs the next step; pairs with the status-change cue
dismiss means the user is done with this parcel; the quietest option, but a later status change goes unseen

signals: panel returns with no user action

sb-presence.text: Enters by animating upward from the bottom screen edge, sits above most elements, and does not block input while visible.
properties: elevation below dialogs and bottom sheets
behaviors: Input elsewhere on the page keeps working while it is up
It is level with the floating action button in elevation, so the button moves up to make room
signals: notice rises from the bottom edge

sb-stacking-core.text: Only one on screen at a time; it times out rather than persisting or stacking, and a core action never lives only in it.
properties: not the only route to a core use
behaviors: A second notice starts only after the first starts contracting downward
A notice that must stay until acted on belongs in a dialog
signals: one notice at a time, no list of them
a second one replaces the first with a downward contraction

sb-exit-timeout.text: Leaves by swipe off-screen, by timing out, or when the user interacts elsewhere, such as opening a new surface.
behaviors: On Android, a focus change from an unrelated popup restarts the timeout so the full duration can be read
signals: notice fades out with no action taken
notice vanishes when another surface opens

sb-distinct-content.reading: transient snackbar: one reading of toast
sb-distinct-content.text: One reading of toast, the transient snackbar: one line tied to the operation just performed, an optional single text action, and no icons. These limits describe that reading only.
behaviors: Two or more actions move the content into a dialog, not a snackbar
A dismiss control counts as an action, so dismiss plus one action also means a dialog
A persistent multi-action panel is a different reading with its own action row; see sb-panel-actions

sb-panel-actions.reading: persistent multi-action panel: another reading of toast
sb-panel-actions.text: The persistent collapsible panel can carry three actions in one row: copy tracking number, open carrier, dismiss. It is a panel reading, so the snackbar limit of zero or one action does not govern it.
behaviors: Three labelled actions fit one row at desktop width
At 375 px the row can wrap or fold into a menu
The panel stays until collapsed or dismissed, so its actions remain reachable while the status changes
signals: panel persists across a status change

m-shared-behaviors.term: how light, elevation and status act in the dark examples
m-shared-behaviors.text: On the dark examples, depth comes from stepping the surface lighter, and the status is carried by a word and a colored tag rather than by color alone.

Large numerals and short labels carry the hierarchy in a small panel
m-shared-behaviors.principle: On dark surfaces, depth and status come from value steps and words, since shadows and hues barely register.
signals: lighter gray step per elevation level

motion._about: Collapse, expand, toast presence, status-change cue, auto-dismiss and reduced motion. Fetched pages give no numeric collapse, expand or toast durations; those are illustrative dials with ranges. Options, not requirements.

mo-toast-presence.text: How the toast arrives and leaves. The fetched Material page sets the direction (up from the bottom edge), not a duration.
mo-toast-presence.quote: Upon entrance, snackbars animate upwards from the bottom edge of the screen.

readings.reading: slide and fade from an edge
readings.in_practice: translate 8-16 px plus opacity 0 to 1, about 200-250 ms, ease-out
scale 0.96 to 1 with a small overshoot, a spring of about 300 ms
no travel; content swaps at once, then a status-change pulse
opacity only, about 150 ms

mo-status-cue.text: When the package status changes while the panel is shown, the change can pulse, flash, reappear as a toast, or update silently. Each signals something different.
behaviors: A pulse of one status word marks the change without pulling focus
A reappearing toast surfaces a change the user may have missed while collapsed
A silent update keeps motion at zero and relies on the new text
mo-status-cue.principle: The cue should say the status changed without asking for an action.

mo-reduced-motion.text: Interaction-triggered animation can be turned off unless it carries information. The alternative keeps the state change and drops the travel.
behaviors: Under reduced motion, expand and collapse become an instant swap of the height
The status cue becomes a text change with no pulse
Opacity-only fades can stay, since they carry no travel
mo-reduced-motion.principle: Reduced motion removes movement, not the information the movement was carrying.
signals: no transform or scale in the reduced branch

mo-collapse-expand.text: Collapse and expand change the panel height and the chevron rotation together, so the face and body stay in step mid-move.
behaviors: A short expand (about 200-300 ms) reads as responsive; past 400 ms the wait starts to feel slow
Collapse can run a little shorter than expand, so the pill returns before the eye leaves it
mo-collapse-expand.principle: Matched timing keeps the disclosure legible as one movement.
signals: height and chevron finish on the same frame
no content jump at the end of the move

mo-sequenced-steps.text: A multi-step size change reads better as a visible timeline than as one jump, so queued steps (see the size transitions entry) are the way to build it.

mo-dismiss-timing.text: A transient toast leaves on a timeout or when the user interacts elsewhere. Search snippets put the timeout at about 4 to 10 seconds, with a Flutter default of 4.

readings.in_practice: dismiss after about 4 to 10 s (5 to 8 s is a middle dial); the timer stops while the pointer is over the panel
timer restarts when focus returns, so the full duration can be read
persistent panel, dismissed only by the user or collapsed

readings.reading: edge strip: one line across a screen edge
readings.in_practice: a 40 to 48 px full-width bar docked to the bottom

readings.reading: small card: status and ETA, no timeline
readings.in_practice: a 200 to 240 px wide card, two lines

readings.reading: progress chip: a ring with a count
readings.in_practice: a round chip about 44 px with a progress ring

senses._about: Ambiguous prompt words and the sense meant here. Excluded senses are scoped anti-keywords at the top level; the readings stay open.

senses.meant: a floating panel over the page
senses.readings_kept: a transient auto-dismissing notification stays available as one reading of toast UI menu

senses.meant: a compact control surface with a few actions

worn_paths._about: What a model given only the prompt would most likely produce for a dark, very compact, collapsible package toast. Each worn path is a generic default; the scoped not_wanted entries in anti_keywords carry the rewrites.

wp-generic-alert.text: A rounded white or grey alert box with a bell and a red X, which reads as an error even when the package is in transit.
behaviors: red X on every state
rounded alert chrome copied from a notification library

wp-neon-purple.text: Dark UI given neon outlines, a glow halo, or a violet-to-pink gradient as the accent.
behaviors: glow on the border
gradient on the status word or the button

wp-bottom-bar.text: A wide bar docked along the bottom of the page with large display type for the status, which is not very compact at all.
behaviors: full viewport width
large headline type in the collapsed state

wp-decoration.text: Emoji stand in for carrier status (a box, a truck, a check) and every row, chip and button carries its own drop shadow.
behaviors: emoji as status icons
shadow on each element, so nothing reads as the one floating panel

wp-halation.text: Pure #fff text on a #000 background, which glows and smears on dark screens (halation) and is harsh for long reading.
behaviors: full-white body text
pure black canvas

wp-hover-only.text: The step list opens only on mouse hover, and the toggle and dismiss controls are 12 to 16 px, too small to hit by touch or keyboard.
behaviors: expand on mouseenter
toggle under 24 px

status_data._about: Derived guesses about the status data (inferred, tier 2): shapes and formats to choose from, not a default. The hard-coded sample in the page is one possible choice; nothing here comes from a fetched carrier API.

sd-status-shape.text: One package as a record: carrier, tracking number, status, eta and a list of checkpoints, with an exception optional. One shape among several.

choices.choice: flat record with checkpoints as a list
choices.fits_when: one parcel in a static demo; the simplest to hard-code in the page

choices.choice: status as a fixed set of words
choices.fits_when: every status maps to a hue and a shopper action; a closed set keeps that mapping complete

choices.choice: status as free text from the carrier
choices.fits_when: the carrier's wording is shown as given; needs a fallback hue for words it does not know
a delay or damage needs a line of its own; otherwise it can live inside the status

sd-checkpoint.text: One checkpoint: a label, a time, a place and a state, with an optional exception note. The options below are alternatives, and none is fixed.

choices.fits_when: the stepper marks the current stage and greys the rest

choices.choice: state as done or pending only
choices.fits_when: the list is history with no 'now' marker

choices.choice: time as a full timestamp with timezone
choices.fits_when: checkpoints span zones or the minute matters

choices.choice: time as a date and time of day
choices.fits_when: a short list where the zone is implied

choices.choice: place as a city and region, or null
choices.fits_when: some scans carry no location; null renders as no place

sd-eta-format.text: The expected delivery shown beside the status word. Each format fits a different level of certainty from the carrier.

choices.fits_when: the carrier gives a day and no time
the carrier gives a range, such as a morning window; shows the range, not a point
delivery is a day or two away and 'tomorrow' reads faster than a date
shown when the viewer may sit in another zone from the parcel; hidden when both share one

s-wcag-target.title: Understanding WCAG 2.2: Target Size (Minimum)
s-wcag-target.quote: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels

s-wcag-contrast.title: Understanding WCAG 2.2: Contrast (Minimum)
s-wcag-contrast.quote: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1

s-wcag-nontext.title: Understanding WCAG 2.2: Non-text Contrast
s-wcag-nontext.quote: Ensure meaningful visual cues achieve 3:1 against the background.

s-wcag-motion.title: Understanding WCAG 2.2: Animation from Interactions
s-wcag-motion.quote: Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential to the functionality or the information being conveyed.

s-ups-statuses.title: UPS Tracking Statuses Explained
s-ups-statuses.quote: Common statuses include Label Created, Shipped/On the Way, Out for Delivery, Delivered, Delivered to a UPS Access Point, and Exception.

s-ups-eta.title: UPS Tracking Statuses Explained
s-ups-eta.quote: current location, status, and expected delivery date

s-ups-exception.title: UPS Tracking Statuses Explained
s-ups-exception.quote: event has interrupted delivery: address issue, recipient unavailable, weather delay, customs hold, or package damage

s-ship24-out.title: What every parcel tracking status actually means
s-ship24-out.quote: On a vehicle for delivery today

s-ship24-label.title: What every parcel tracking status actually means
s-ship24-label.quote: The carrier does not have the parcel

s-ship24-exception.title: What every parcel tracking status actually means
s-ship24-exception.quote: Catch-all for anything off the expected path

s-ship24-action.title: What every parcel tracking status actually means

s-material-contrast.title: Material Design 2: Dark theme
s-material-contrast.quote: Primary colors are desaturated so they pass the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines’ (WCAG) AA standard of at least 4.5:1

s-wcag-large.title: Understanding WCAG 2.2: Contrast (Minimum)
s-wcag-large.quote: Large-scale text and images of large-scale text have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1

s-mdui-placement.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-placement.quote: Snackbars appear above most elements on screen

s-mdui-entrance.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-entrance.quote: Upon entrance, snackbars animate upwards from the bottom edge of the screen.

s-mdui-noblock.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-noblock.quote: When they appear, they do not block input.

s-mdui-exit.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-exit.quote: automatically disappear after a timeout or user interaction elsewhere

s-mdui-android-reset.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-android-reset.quote: the snackbar timeout will reset upon the window focus being regained

s-mdui-one-line.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-one-line.quote: Snackbars should contain a single line of text directly related to the operation performed.

s-mdui-actions.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-actions.quote: For two or more actions, use a dialog, not a snackbar, even when one of the actions is a dismiss action.

s-mdui-one-at-time.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-one-at-time.quote: Show only one snackbar on screen at a time.

s-mdui-not-persistent.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-not-persistent.quote: They should not be persistent or be stacked, as they are above other elements on screen.

s-mdui-consecutive.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-consecutive.quote: the first should start the contraction motion downwards before the second one animates upwards

s-mdui-core.title: Snackbars & toasts - Components - Material Design 1
s-mdui-core.quote: should not contain the only way to access a core use case
